Why Junior’s

A chimney gives you no warning. It just waits.

A hairline crack in a flue tile. A crown that has quietly given up. A quarter inch of glazed creosote you cannot see from the hearth. None of it announces itself in your living room — until the day it does, and it costs you a ceiling, a claim, or worse.

Junior has spent thirty years learning to read the things homeowners never see. Every visit starts with a real inspection and a straight answer — not a sales pitch, and not a scare. If your chimney is fine, we will tell you it is fine.

The part you never see

Six places a chimney quietly fails.

Hover any point on the cutaway. This is what Junior is actually looking at when he is up there — and what a $199 “special” from a call centre never checks.

01 · The cap

Missing or rusted caps let rain, leaves, squirrels and birds straight into the flue. It is the cheapest part of the whole system and the one that causes the most expensive damage when it is gone.

02 · The crown

The concrete slab on top. Once it cracks, water runs down inside the masonry, freezes, and takes the brickwork apart from within. Most crowns in Bucks County are past due for a rebuild.

03 · The flue liner

The barrier between a 1,000°F fire and the timber framing of your house. Cracked clay tile, gaps in the mortar joints, or a flue oversized for a new furnace all mean the same thing: it needs relining.

04 · The flashing

Where the chimney meets the roof. Nine out of ten “chimney leaks” we get called about are failed flashing or unsealed masonry — not the roof, and not the flue.

05 · The damper & smoke chamber

A seized damper wastes heat all winter and will not close in a chimney fire. A rough, unparged smoke chamber is where creosote loves to build — and where most fires actually start.

06 · The firebox

Spalled firebrick and open mortar joints put heat directly against the structure behind them. It is visible from your living room and almost nobody looks.

Service 01

Chimney Sweeping & Inspection

The job everything else depends on. Rotary brushes and rods through the full flue, a HEPA vacuum running the entire time, and a proper Level 1 inspection of the system from cap to firebox.

What you get

Creosote and soot removed from the full flue, the smoke chamber and the firebox. Damper cleaned and checked for free travel. Cap, crown and flashing inspected. Photos of anything that needs your attention.

How long

About an hour for a standard fireplace. Heavier build-up or a glazed flue takes longer — we will tell you before we start, not after.

The mess

There isn’t any. Drop cloths on the hearth and the floor, HEPA extraction at the source, and a wipe-down before we leave.

Book a sweep

Service 02

Chimney Relining

This is Junior’s speciality. When the clay tile inside your chimney has cracked, or the flue is oversized for a newer high-efficiency furnace, the only real answer is a properly sized stainless liner.

When you need one

Cracked or shifted flue tiles. A chimney fire in the history of the house. A furnace, boiler or water heater swapped for a high-efficiency unit. A wood stove insert. Or a failed certification.

Why it matters

The liner is the only thing between combustion gases and the wood framing of your house. A cracked flue leaks carbon monoxide into living space and heat into your walls.

How we do it

Sized to the appliance, insulated where code requires it, top plate and cap installed, and the whole system tested before we call it done. Most jobs finish in a day.

Ask about relining

Service 03

Chimney Repairs

Water is what actually destroys chimneys — not fire. Almost every repair we do traces back to something letting rain in and freeze-thaw doing the rest.

A

Crown rebuilds

Cracked or crumbling crowns cut out and recast properly, with an overhang and a drip edge so water sheds instead of soaking in.

B

Flashing & leaks

Step and counter flashing replaced and sealed where the stack meets the roof. Most “roof leaks” near a chimney start right here.

C

Caps & dampers

Stainless caps with spark arrestor mesh, and dampers that actually seal — including top-sealing dampers that stop winter heat loss.

D

Tuckpointing

Failed mortar joints ground out and repointed to match. Done before the brick starts moving, it is a fraction of a rebuild.

E

Waterproofing

Breathable masonry sealer that keeps rain out while letting the chimney dry — the cheapest insurance on the whole stack.

F

Firebox repair

Spalled firebrick replaced and joints repointed with refractory mortar rated for the temperatures it actually sees.

Straight answers

Questions we get every week.

How often does a chimney actually need sweeping?

Once a year for anything you burn regularly — wood, pellet, gas or oil. Wood burners who go through more than a cord a season should have it looked at mid-winter too. If you have not burned in it at all this year, you still want it inspected: most problems we find are water and animal damage, not soot.

What does it cost?

You get a flat price before any work starts, and it does not change unless you agree to something extra. Estimates are free. Pricing depends on the height of the stack, what is being burned and how much build-up is in there — which is why we quote it honestly instead of advertising a bait price.

Do you make a mess?

No. Drop cloths go down before anything else, a HEPA vacuum runs at the firebox the whole time, and the hearth gets wiped down before we leave. Junior has been doing this for thirty years specifically so nobody has to clean up after him.

My chimney is leaking. Is that a roof problem?

Usually not. Nine times out of ten it is failed flashing where the stack meets the roof, a cracked crown, or porous brick that has never been sealed. We will tell you honestly if it is actually your roof — we would rather send you to a roofer than sell you a repair that does not fix it.

Can you do a certification before my settlement?

Yes, and quickly. Tell us your closing date when you call. You get a written, signed certification with photos, and if anything fails you get a quote to correct it in the same visit so the deal keeps moving.

Are you insured?

Fully insured, and happy to send a certificate of insurance to you, your agent or your township before we start. Every cleaning is performed by a Certified Chimney Professional technician.

The story

Thirty years of learning what a chimney is about to do.

Junior has been working on chimneys and masonry for three decades — long enough to walk up to a stack from the driveway and already have a fair idea of what he is going to find on top of it.

He opened Junior’s Chimney in 2018 to do it his own way: one certified technician on every job, honest pricing quoted up front, and a house left cleaner than he found it. No subcontractors. No pressure. No inventing problems that are not there.

That is why almost every job on the calendar comes from a repeat customer or a neighbour they sent. Real estate agents keep his number for settlements. Insurance adjusters ask for him by name. And people who have been burned by a cheap “$99 special” tend to stay a very long time once they find him.

Certified Chimney Professional

Every cleaning is performed by a certified technician with a minimum of fifteen years in the trade — and in Junior’s case, thirty.

Certified relining specialist

Stainless liners sized, insulated and installed to code. It is the work most sweeps refer out, and it is what Junior is known for.

Fully insured

Certificate of insurance available before we start — to you, your agent, or your township.

Open seven days

8:00am to 6:00pm, Monday through Sunday. Weekend appointments are normal here, not a favour.

Four rules we don’t bend.

If your chimney is fine, we say so and we go home. Nobody has ever been talked into a repair in this company’s history, and nobody ever will be.

The equipment

Professional tools, not a shop vac.

The difference between a real sweep and a cheap one is almost entirely in what comes out of the truck.

HEPA extraction

Negative-pressure vacuum at the firebox for the entire job, so fine soot never enters your living space instead of settling on it later.

Rotary flue systems

Powered rotary heads for glazed creosote that a hand brush will not touch — the build-up that actually starts chimney fires.

Inspection camera

Photos and video of the inside of your flue. You see what we see, instead of taking our word for it.

Full masonry kit

Mixers, grinders, scaffold and refractory materials on the truck, so a repair does not become a second appointment three weeks out.
